newsitem.title: Bangladesh: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Bangladesh's police has sought help from the Interpol in tracing the whereabouts of fugitives accused in the murder of independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in 1975.

Tribal insurgents Shanti Bahini has unilaterally extended the truce in Chittagong Hill Tracts until November 30. Rebels issued a press release on Sunday announcing the extension of the ceasefire, expired on October 31.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has reiterated that the trial of Independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman will be held "on the soil of Bangladesh". "None would be able to protect the killers," she said.
Five more service sectors including electricity and transport are likely to be included in the Valued Aded Tax (VAT) net within the current fiscal year, ending June.

Police has arrested Zobaida Rashid, wife of retired army colonel Abdur Rashid who is accused of killing independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in 1975 and now absconding. Mrs Rashid was arrested on charge of keeping illegal arms.
Bangladesh (central) Bank, in a major step towards cooling down the overheated stock market, has asked scheduled banks to stop giving loans against share certificates.
Four companies will soon go to the buoyant capital market offering Initial Public Offerings (IPOs) worth 594 million taka ($14.5 million).
